description: Cut 1-4 regions from a full-resolution render of a photo with its current Develop settings, one rendered pixel per returned pixel, to judge sharpness of a detail such as the nearest eye. The render is a temporary export (JPEG quality 100, sRGB, output sharpening off, no catalog add), deleted before the call returns (one left by a timed-out or cancelled call, by a later detail call); it takes seconds, and a render that starts while another export or detail render runs is refused, not queued. Its first step reads the cropped frame and waits for the Develop calls before it, as every read of a photo's develop state does; the render runs alongside them. Each call adds one Export history step to the photo and marks it exported, so summarize_develop_settings' exported_only counts it; Develop settings and pixels stay unchanged unless Lightroom's AI Updates Recommended dialog is answered with "Update affected photos" checked, which first updates the AI masks, and no cached preview, selection or module changes. Returns photo_id, crop_jpeg_quality (95), per region its pixel box in the render and the image (JPEG 95), plus render {width, height, jpeg_quality, color_space, output_sharpening, source, left_on_photo}: source says how the render was made, a string ("export" today); left_on_photo says what the render left on the photo, a list of phrases ("one Export history step", "the exported mark"). A region larger than max_edge, measured against the cropped frame get_crop reports, is refused before the render with the largest normalized size this photo allows; nothing is scaled. A call refused before the render (unknown photo, the cropped frame not read, region over max_edge, export running) is failed with nothing left; an error once the render started is unknown and names the export and what it leaves on the photo. Rules: every region must fit within the rendered frame (x + width and y + height at most 1).

max_edge.description: Largest region edge in pixels (default 1024). Keep it within what your model receives without downscaling; the server cannot know that limit.

photo_ids.description: One photo ID or file path

regions.description: Rectangles in the displayed frame after develop crop and rotation, normalized like get_photo_preview's region; pixel bounds round outward
